events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 8 feet Friday, increasing to 8 to 12 feet Saturday. Surf heights are expected to decrease to 5 to 9 feet Sunday through Tuesday. Dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. Surf will we highest for west-northwest facing beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 PM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM to 4 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas that are normally dry, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of significant west- northwesterly swells are expected to produce large surf into next week with highest surf and greatest impacts likely peaking Saturday and potentially again Monday. Minor to moderate coastal flooding impacts are possible, especially when largest surf overlaps with peak high tides. Some of these impacts may be moderate to significant beach erosion and shallow flooding of normally dry beaches and walkways.

location.region: Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches

events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 18 to 25 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to 15 feet with dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until 3 AM PST Sunday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 3 AM Sunday to 3 PM PST Tuesday. * IMPACTS...Powerful waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers and jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of west-northwesterly swells will create an extended period of large surf into next week, with the potential for WARNING level surf again late Sunday night through Monday. Areas that may see most significant impacts will be west- northwest facing beaches, with widespread flooding likely at low lying areas such as at Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may impact the Cayucos and Pismo Beach piers as well as the Morro Bay Harbor entrance.

water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.

necessary, drive with extreme caution and be prepared for sudden
changes in visibility. Leave plenty of room between you and the
motorist ahead of you, and allow extra time to reach your
destination. Avoid sudden braking or acceleration, and be especially
cautious on hills or when making turns. Make sure your car is
winterized and in good working order.

weather.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. The latest road conditions
for the state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Monitor the latest forecasts for updates on this situation.

Persons are urged to stay indoors until conditions improve. If you
must go outside, dress in layers. Several layers of clothes will keep
you warmer than a single heavy coat. Cover exposed skin to reduce
your risk of frostbite or hypothermia. Gloves, a scarf, and a hat
will keep you from losing your body heat.

Persons should consider delaying all travel. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution. Consider taking a winter storm
kit along with you, including such items as tire chains, booster
cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets and extra clothing. Also take
water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.

from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM CST

night.

those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will be unable
to be driven on the beach. This includes locations north of

expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best

weather.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...Aransas Islands, Kleberg Islands, Nueces Islands and Calhoun Islands Counties. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 9 AM CST Tuesday. For the High Rip Current Risk, through Tuesday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even the most experienced swimmers away from shore into deeper water. These rip currents can become life-threatening to anyone entering the surf.

location.region: Aransas Islands; Kleberg Islands; Nueces Islands; Calhoun Islands

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 16 at 4:49PM CST until November 17 at 6:00PM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Aransas Islands, Kleberg Islands, Nueces Islands and
Calhoun Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 9 AM CST Tuesday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even
the most experienced swimmers away from shore into deeper
water. These rip currents can become life-threatening to
anyone entering the surf.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.
weather.areaDesc: Aransas Islands; Kleberg Islands; Nueces Islands; Calhoun Islands

weather.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

shore and call or wave for help.

weather.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip current.

* WHERE...Beaches along the northwest to northeast coastline of
Puerto Rico, including beaches in Aguada and Rincon.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
weather.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

in case you become stranded.

weather.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 17 at 1:28AM EST until November 19 at 1:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 10
feet expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Thursday
evening. For the High Surf Advisory, from 7 PM this evening to
1 PM EST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.
weather.areaDesc: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible. * WHERE...Most of east central Florida, including Volusia, Seminole, Orange, Osceola, Okeechobee, Brevard, Indian River, Saint Lucie, and Martin counties. * WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Friday evening. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - Repeated rounds of showers and isolated storms are forecast through Friday. Rainfall amounts of 3 to 6 inches are forecast with localized higher amounts of 8 to 12 inches. The greatest potential for these higher amounts will be over the coastal counties. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

weather.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Most of east central Florida, including Volusia, Seminole,
Orange, Osceola, Okeechobee, Brevard, Indian River, Saint Lucie,
and Martin counties.

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Repeated rounds of showers and isolated storms are forecast
through Friday. Rainfall amounts of 3 to 6 inches are forecast
with localized higher amounts of 8 to 12 inches. The greatest
potential for these higher amounts will be over the coastal
counties.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

Winds will gust as high as 65 mph, reducing visibility to one quarter mile or less. * WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island. * WHEN...From 3 PM Tuesday to 1 AM AKST Wednesday. * IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Very strong winds could cause extensive damage to power lines. Visibilities reduced to one quarter mile or less due to blowing snow. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A strong Bering storm arrives at the Southwest Coast on Tuesday, bringing gusty southerly winds. Temperatures are expected to warm Wednesday morning, allowing for a transition to mixed precipitation.

location.region: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island

weather.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 16 at 1:31PM AKST until November 18 at 1:00AM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
weather.description:
* WHAT...Blizzard conditions expected. Total snow accumulations of 1
to 3 inches. Winds will gust as high as 65 mph, reducing visibility
to one quarter mile or less.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island.

* WHEN...From 3 PM Tuesday to 1 AM AKST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Very strong winds could
cause extensive damage to power lines. Visibilities reduced to one
quarter mile or less due to blowing snow.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A strong Bering storm arrives at the Southwest
Coast on Tuesday, bringing gusty southerly winds. Temperatures are
expected to warm Wednesday morning, allowing for a transition to
mixed precipitation.
weather.instruction:
A Winter Storm Warning for snow means severe winter weather
conditions will make travel very hazardous. If you must travel, keep
an extra flashlight, food and water in your vehicle in case of an
emergency.

Do not touch downed lines and report any power outages to your
electric company. Travel is highly discouraged due to slick roadways
and the possibility of downed trees and power lines.
weather.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Large waves of 25 to 30 feet may impact Saint Paul, including the harbor area. * WHERE...West Saint Paul * WHEN...9 AM Tuesday to Noon Wednesday. * IMPACTS...Large waves may result in water overtopping the breakwater at Saint Paul Harbor, leading to minor flooding of low-lying coastal areas, particularly near the harbor. Coastal erosion is possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Prolonged gusty southeasterly winds will shift to gusty westerly winds as the storm progresses east.

location.region: Pribilof Islands

weather.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 16 at 12:12PM AKST until November 18 at 12:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
weather.description:
* WHAT...Large waves of 25 to 30 feet may impact Saint Paul,
including the harbor area.

* WHERE...West Saint Paul

* WHEN...9 AM Tuesday to Noon Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Large waves may result in water overtopping the
breakwater at Saint Paul Harbor, leading to minor flooding of
low-lying coastal areas, particularly near the harbor. Coastal
erosion is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Prolonged gusty southeasterly winds will
shift to gusty westerly winds as the storm progresses east.
weather.instruction:
Precautions should be taken to protect property. Stay away from
beaches, shorelines, and harbor areas.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Coastal Flooding with water levels of 1.0 to 3.0 feet above the highest tide line possible. * WHERE...Kipnuk and Kwigillingok. * WHEN...3 AM to 9 AM Wednesday. * IMPACTS...Potential flooding of low lying areas, including overtop the lowest portions of boardwalks. Coastal erosion possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A long duration of gusty southerly winds will move through the Kuskokwim Coast on Tuesday. Winds turn more south to southwesterly Wednesday, increasing the potential for elevated water levels, high surf, and coastal erosion. The winds will coincide with the high tide on Wednesday morning.

* Special Marine Warning for...
Straits of Florida from Halfmoon Shoal to 20 nm west of Dry

* Until 515 PM EST.

* At 420 PM EST, a possible strong waterspout was located 19 nm
southeast of Tortugas Ecological Reserve South, moving east at 10
knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts, wind gusts 34 knots or greater, and large
hail.

SOURCE...National Weather Service Meteorologist.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats, cause
considerable damage to vessels and create suddenly higher
waves. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly
higher waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours.
Large hail could result in injury and damage to boats.

weather.instruction:

seas, frequent lightning, and blinding downpours. Stay low or go
below, and make sure all on board are wearing life jackets.

seas. Seek safe harbor immediately.

weather.instruction:
Prepare for thunderstorms with wind gusts near 30 knots, locally
rough and confused seas, occasional lightning strikes, and
potentially blinding downpours. Get to a safe port as quickly, and as
safely as possible. When downpours reduce visibility, slow down.

Frequent lightning is occurring with these storms. Stay low, or go
below. Lower VHF antenna, outriggers, fishing rods, and umbrellas.
Avoid open areas on islands and sandbars. Do not shelter under tall
or isolated trees on nearby mangrove islands.

events.title: Winter Storm Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Heavy snow expected in the Eastern Sierra. For elevations between 5,000 and 8,000 feet, storm total snow accumulations of 10 to 18 inches expected. For elevations between 8,000 and 9,500 feet, storm total snow accumulations of 18 to 36 inches expected. Locally higher totals expected above 9,500 feet. weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 17 at 4:50PM AST until November 18 at 12:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
weather.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip current.

* WHERE...Beaches along the northwest to northeast coastline of
Puerto Rico, including beaches in Aguada and Rincon.

* WHEN...Through late Wednesday morning.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
weather.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

events.description: * WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 12 to 17 ft. For the High Surf Advisory, Large breaking waves of 15 to 18 ft along the coast from Wednesday afternoon through Thursday afternoon. * WHERE...San Francisco County. * WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Wednesday afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 5 AM Wednesday to 10 AM PST Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM Wednesday to 4 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to be 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 6:53 AM Wednesday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 7
feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM CST
Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 6 AM CST
Wednesday. For the High Rip Current Risk, until 6 AM CST

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching
or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations
north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach
erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions
and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Max inundation is expected near high tide
at 1105 PM tonight and again at 1049 PM Thursday night.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 11 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 AM EST Friday. For the High Rip Current Risk, through Thursday evening. * IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

weather.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 17 at 2:24PM EST until November 20 at 7:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 11 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 AM EST Friday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.
weather.areaDesc: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands

events.description: The officials at the Indiana Department of Environmental Management have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory for Elkhart County, in effect from 6 PM this evening to 10 AM EST Wednesday. A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM 2.5 has been issued due to stagnant conditions and calm winds. Fine particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups range. Active children and adults, and people with respiratory disease, such as asthma should limit prolonged outdoor exposure. Due to observed and forecasted high concentration of PM2.5 readings in the area, recommendations are for the public to reduce or avoid exertion or heavy work outdoors and keep windows and doors closed as much as possible. For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at: http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties. .On the St Johns River at Astor, slight rises within Minor Flood Stage are forecast through at least midweek due to a combination of northerly winds and water from upstream heavy rainfall working north through the basin. Rises to Moderate Flood Stage are forecast later in the week due to the additional heavy rainfall expected. For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor to Moderate flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Astor. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 8:30 AM EST Tuesday the stage was 2.7 feet. - Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 8:30 AM EST Tuesday was 2.7 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.4 feet Sunday morning. Additional rises are possible thereafter. - Flood stage is 2.3 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: Air Quality Alert
events.description: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection has issued a code ORANGE air quality alert for Tuesday, for the Mon Valley area. A code ORANGE air quality alert means that air pollution concentrations within the region may become unhealthy for sensitive groups. Sensitive groups include children, the elderly, and people suffering from asthma, heart disease, or other lung diseases. The effects of air pollution can be minimized by avoiding outdoor exercise or strenuous activity. For more information on ground-level ozone and fine particles, visit http://www.airnow.gov and https://www.ahs.dep.pa.gov/AQPartnersWeb/

events.title: Rip Current Statement
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 12 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...Coastal Palm Beach County and Coastal Broward County. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM EST Thursday. For the High Rip Current Risk, through Thursday evening. * IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

location.region: Coastal Palm Beach County; Coastal Broward County

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 17 at 8:09AM EST until November 19 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7
to 12 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Palm Beach County and Coastal Broward County.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM EST Thursday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.
weather.areaDesc: Coastal Palm Beach County; Coastal Broward County

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be possible. * WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following areas, Coastal Broward County, Coastal Miami Dade County, Coastal Palm Beach County, Far South Miami-Dade County, Inland Broward County, Inland Miami-Dade County, Inland Palm Beach County, Metro Broward County, Metro Palm Beach County and Metropolitan Miami Dade. * WHEN...From 1 PM EST this afternoon through Thursday evening. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - Several rounds of storms may produce rainfall amounts of 2 to 4 inches through late Thursday. Higher amounts of 6 to 8 inches with locally isolated amounts over 10 inches may be possible. Heavy rainfall rates of 1 to 2 inches per hour may observed with some of these storms. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: High Wind Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Southeast winds 45 to 55 mph with gusts to 75 mph; winds turn westerly beginning Tuesday evening. * WHERE...Pribilof Islands. * WHEN...Until 9 AM AKST Wednesday. * IMPACTS...High winds may move loose debris, damage property, and cause power outages. Travel will be difficult. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds have increased in strength overnight, and are expected to peak later this morning as a strong low pressure system moves through the Bering. A short lull of high winds will occur before a second peak in westerly winds occurs Tuesday evening through Wednesday morning with winds gusting to 75 mph. As a result of the long duration of westerly winds, wave heights of 25 to 30 ft within 15 to 20 nautical miles of Saint Paul are expected through Wednesday afternoon.

location.region: Pribilof Islands
